c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: The car finds a torch across the room. What does it actually know about where the light is?

C.text: Only whether it is bright right now or not

D.text: Its exact position on the floor

c1.why: One sensor gives one number. Direction is not measured — it is found by turning until the number changes.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: Why does the car spin when it is dark?

A.text: To warn people it is lost

C.text: Spinning is how it searches for a bright direction

c2.why: A car that cannot measure direction can still find one — by facing every direction in turn and checking each.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: Only one light sensor, and yet the car finds a direction. How?

B.text: It remembers where the light was last lesson

C.text: It uses the sonar as a second sensor

D.text: It turns, so the one sensor faces different ways over time

c3.why: Turning trades time for a second sensor. Facing a new way and re-reading gives the comparison a second sensor would have given.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: The room is dark and no torch is on. What does the car do?
r1.why: The reading is below the threshold, so the search branch runs and keeps running.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: You switch on a torch and point it at the car. What happens?

C.text: It stops spinning and drives towards the light

r2.why: The reading rises above the threshold, the test fails, and the `else` branch drives the car straight ahead.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: The car is driving towards the torch and you switch it off. What does it do?

B.text: Carries on to where the light was

r3.why: The loop re-reads the sensor constantly, so the moment the light goes the car falls back into the search branch.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: The threshold is set to 200 in a normal classroom. What does the car do?

A.text: Keeps spinning unless a torch is held right up to the screen

r4.why: Almost every reading in an ordinary room is below 200, so the test is almost always true and the car only leaves the search when a torch is right up against the screen.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: This car drives away in the dark and spins when you shine a torch on it — backwards. Which change fixes it?
d1.why: The test is right; the two behaviors are in the wrong branches. Dark should search, bright should drive.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car picks one behavior at start-up and never changes. What is missing?
d2.why: Seeking only works if the sensor is read again and again. Asked once, the car is stuck with whatever the room was at start-up.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: What are the two behaviors a light-seeking car needs?

B.text: Search when dark, drive when bright

C.text: Drive when dark, stop when bright

D.text: Search when bright, reverse when dark

b1.why: Two behaviors, chosen by one test. That pairing is what makes the car look like it is hunting.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: You measure your room: about 15 with the lights off, about 90 with them on. Which threshold should you use?
b2.why: A threshold belongs between the two readings. Sitting on top of one of them makes the car flicker between behaviors.
